record: Senné Roman Catholic register: baptisms, marriages, burials
covers: Roman Catholics of Senné and of its filials. In this title: baptisms 1866-1912, marriages 1863-1926, deaths 1831-1925.
held: State archive, Prešov. Filmed in 1993: FamilySearch catalogue 710997, films 1793682 and 1793683 (image groups 4407158 and 4407159).
note: The catalogue page was read in the research pass. The span 1831-1926 hides a gap: baptisms in this title begin only in 1866. Earlier baptisms are in the older set, PL-R-006.

record: Iňačovce Roman Catholic entries
covers: Roman Catholics living in Iňačovce
held: State archive, Prešov
note: Listed as kept in another parish, which fits Senné. Its start year, 1863, matches the first marriage volume in the Senné title (PL-R-001), so this is probably the same book under another heading. Iňačovce is missing from the Senné parish's list of filials for 1917.

record: Iňačovce Greek Catholic register
covers: Greek Catholics of the parish district: Iňačovce, Jastrabie, Senné and Stretava
held: State archive, Prešov
note: The parish's own book, kept from 1811 and held at Prešov, reportedly complete to 1898. No later volume is in the state archive. The church archive was badly damaged by lightning in 1929 and fire in 1930, so whether the volumes of 1899 onward survive, with the parish or at a registry office, is not known. Burials are not in the index seen, only births and marriages.

record: Greek Catholic records of the Mukachevo eparchy, Ungvár and Ung district
covers: Multiple parishes of the Ung district. Whether Solymos is among them is not checked (PL-H-005).
held: Zakarpattia state archive, Uzhhorod and Berehove. Filmed: FamilySearch catalogue 1411329.
note: The likeliest home for a Greek Catholic baptism from Iňačovce after 1898.

record: Iňačovce Reformed register
years: 1747-1940 by one list; 1819-1927 for births by another
covers: The Reformed of Iňačovce
held: State archive, Prešov. Kept at the Reformed mother church of Lúčky.
note: The Reformed of Iňačovce were a filial of Lúčky and are entered in the Lúčky book. An index gives births 1819-1927 and marriages 1820-1926 and two film groups, 4406775 and 4406804, which are probably this book. The start year 1747 is not confirmed.

record: Senné Roman Catholic register, older volumes
years: 1793-1878 indexed; 1778 said to be the oldest known
covers: Baptisms, marriages and deaths before the volumes in PL-R-001
held: Not yet traced to a catalogue entry. Image groups 4948283 and 4948284 in an index of FamilySearch holdings.
online: FamilySearch images, if the groups are open
note: The municipal history says the oldest known registers date from 1778 and that books from 1718 are mentioned in older writing but unknown today. One list gives the filmed span as 1787-1943. An index page also showed image groups with entries from 1709 near the Senné heading, which may belong to another parish.

record: Čičarovce (Csicser) Greek Catholic register
covers: Greek Catholics of Čičarovce and its filials: Vysoká nad Uhom, Pavlovce nad Uhom, Vojany, Beša, Ižkovce, Križany, Liesková
held: State archive, Prešov, church registers catalogue: no. 180 (1789-1829), no. 181 (1830-1856), no. 182 (births and marriages 1857-1886, deaths 1851-1886; film 40-41), no. 182/1 (births 1887-1904, marriages 1887-1906, deaths 1887-1907; microfilm 432)
online: two FamilySearch image groups reported, 4406715 and 4406819; not checked
note: This is the book for a Viszoka baptism of 1882: volume no. 182. Burials for the fifteen years after it are in no. 182 to 1886 and in no. 182/1 from 1887. No. 180 contains a list of the parish's priests from 1781 to 1941.

record: Čičarovce Roman Catholic and Reformed registers
covers: Roman Catholics of Čičarovce and its filials, which did not include Vysoká; the Reformed of Čičarovce
held: State archive, Prešov: Roman Catholic nos. 174 to 179/1 (films 39-40, microfilm 430); Reformed nos. 183 and 183/1 (film 41, microfilm 432)
note: Listed so nobody searches them for a Viszoka Catholic: those are at Pavlovce (PL-R-052).

record: Pavlovce nad Uhom Roman Catholic register
covers: Roman Catholics of Pavlovce and its filials, Vysoká nad Uhom among them
held: State archive, Prešov, volumes 795 to 798; FamilySearch catalogue 706219, three reels. Earlier births reported at the archdiocesan archive, Košice.
online: FamilySearch catalogue; film numbers not obtained
note: The other rite's book for a mixed couple of Viszoka. By one index the Prešov volumes hold births 1869-1896, marriages 1818-1897 and deaths 1878-1907, which leaves births of 1828 to 1868 unaccounted for.

record: Belža (Bölzse) Greek Catholic register
covers: Greek Catholics of Belža and its filials, Gyňov and Seňa among them
held: State archive, Košice, collection of church registers; filmed in 1994
note: By one index: births 1791-1896, marriages 1830-1890, deaths 1833-1896. The copies of 1894 and 1895 held by the Duska agent fall inside the run, so the originals should be here.

record: Kechnec Roman Catholic register; Seňa Reformed register
covers: Roman Catholics of Kechnec, Milhosť and Seňa; the Reformed of Seňa
held: Seňa Reformed: State archive, Košice, inventory volume II, item 741. Kechnec: by a register index.
note: For the non-Greek-Catholic side of a Seňa household.

record: State registers of births, marriages and deaths
covers: Everyone, whatever the church
held: Registry office for the village; books pass to the state archive 100 years after their last entry. For Solymos in 1906 the registrar sat at Alsókánya (Jastrabie).
note: Start date confirmed: Law XXXIII of 1894, in force 1 October 1895. Three birth volumes of the Senné state register, 1895-1898, 1898-1900 and 1901-1906, appear in an index of FamilySearch image groups (5847168 to 5847170); not yet opened. The registry district and today's registry office are still to be found. A state birth entry of 23 August 1906 for Solymos is headed as done at Alsókánya (a probable reading, DM-D-008). Whether Szenna used the same office is not known.

record: Tax censuses of 1715 and 1720
covers: Heads of taxed households. Senné: 5, then 11. Iňačovce: 8, then 11.
held: Hungarian National Archives, Budapest
online: Hungarian National Archives database (record 7273 for Ung county, 1715)
note: With so few households, each village's list is a dozen names at most. Worth reading in full for both surnames.

record: Maria Theresa urbarial survey
covers: Landlords, with counts of villeins and cottars. The tenant-level tables behind them name each household.
held: Hungarian National Archives, Budapest
note: Senné: 13.5 sessions and 446 acres, 26 villein households under four landlords. Iňačovce: 35 under three. The date of the survey is from training, not from the page.

record: Urbaria et Conscriptiones, E 156: fasc. 044 no. 024; fasc. 121 nos. 012 and 014
covers: No. 012 describes Solymos among other Ung villages; no. 014 values an estate that includes Szenna
held: Hungarian National Archives, Budapest
note: Fasc. 044 no. 024 describes Szenna with a noble manor, farm buildings, demesne meadow and seven deserted half-holdings, beside Palócz, Solymos and Rebrin. The two fasc. 121 items seen in the first batch could not be found again in the research pass. No dates read yet.

record: Land census of 1828
covers: Taxed householders. Senné had 120 houses, Iňačovce 119.
held: Hungarian National Archives, Budapest
note: Only the totals have been seen so far.

record: Census of 1869, household sheets for Ung county
covers: Every person, by house. Whether the sheets for Szenna and Solymos survive is not confirmed (PL-H-006).
held: State Archive of Zakarpattia Oblast, Berehove branch; reported as fond 7/2, sheets for 214 Ung settlements
note: Three independent reports now agree that the Ung county sheets are in the Zakarpattia archive and have not been filmed by FamilySearch. The fond number comes from a survey whose authors marked it as to be checked. Not confirmed for Szenna by name.

record: Czechoslovak census of 1930, household sheets
covers: Every person, by house number, with birthplace, religion and nationality
held: Slovak National Archives, Bratislava
note: Coverage for the two villages not yet checked. This is where a Senné house number can be tested directly.

record: Lexikón obcí Slovenskej republiky
covers: Totals only: Senné 171 houses and 839 people, Iňačovce 190 houses and 747 people
held: Published
online: figures republished by the Nation's Memory Institute
note: No names. Useful as proof that both villages were in Slovakia, and as a ceiling for house numbers.

record: List of churches and parishes, 1733; canonical visitations of 1734 and 1746
covers: Each parish: church, priest, filials, head counts by confession
held: Archdiocesan archive, Eger
online: published in part in three articles
note: No villagers named in what has been published. Fixes the parish map of the 18th century.

record: Greek Catholic parish reorganisation papers, Ung county
covers: Each Greek Catholic parish with its daughter villages and numbers of souls
held: Published source edition, 624 pages, free PDF
note: The catalogue record was seen; the file needs the owner's approval to open from here. The named test for PL-H-001.

record: Parish copy-book of the Bishop of Szatmár's circulars
covers: Ten openings in the Duska agent's Folder 1
held: Not yet known; presumed filmed with the Senné register
note: See the note against DUS:H-010 below: Stretavka was inside the Senné parish in 1734.

record: Senné parish chronicle (kept by Štefan Halás) and the manor diary
covers: Parish and estate life as recorded locally
held: Chronicle: presumably the parish. Diary: location unknown.
online: no; quoted on the municipal website
note: Both are cited by the municipal history. Neither has been seen.

record: Vécsey family papers, with the Ungszenna estate
covers: Estate management, land reform, staff. Tenants and labourers may be named.
held: Romanian National Archives, Cluj county branch, fond 452
note: The article that cites the fond is about the owner, so what it holds on villagers is unknown.

record: Fond Užská župa at Prešov
covers: Mostly Uzhhorod: census sheets, voter lists, some duplicate registers for villages now in Ukraine
held: State archive, Prešov
note: Small fond, 5 boxes. Neither village appears in the finding aid as read. The scan's text layer is poor, so this is a weak negative.
